solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Colour scheme in side corridor

indicators.note: 'in' says the letters sit inside the run of words side corridor, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: An interior designer picks paint for the corridor along the side of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: The decor of a room is its decoration and furnishing style, including the chosen palette of hues.

clue.text: Prepare training information

parts.note: to do a dish or a room is to prepare it
PE is physical education, training in school sport

explanation.surface: A coach gets ready the facts about a training session.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is British school shorthand for physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for inside knowledge, the facts or gen about something.

clue.text: Suck up to groom with act of kindness

parts.note: to curry a horse is to groom it with a currycomb
a favour is an act of kindness

explanation.surface: A flatterer tries to win over a stable lad with a good deed.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingratiate oneself is the idiom's meaning, the same as fawning on someone.

clue.text: Royal English feast

parts.note: regal means royal

explanation.surface: A banquet fit for the English monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale someone is to entertain them lavishly, to feast them.

clue.text: Material needed by friend, organ cleaner

parts.note: cotton is a fabric, a material
bud is American slang for a friend, short for buddy

explanation.surface: A dressmaker needs fabric from a pal; the tail end is a stray phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks musical but is the ear, the body organ the swab is used on.
explanation.definitionFit: A swab on a stick is used to clean ears, the organ of hearing.

clue.text: State capital in New England, a leader in trade pact

parts.note: Concord is the capital of New Hampshire, a New England state

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter, so the opening letter of trade is taken

explanation.surface: A New England capital and a trade chief sign a trade agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A concordat is a formal agreement, especially one between the Vatican and a state.

clue.text: Starts to time his round, old bobby's beat

indicators.note: the starts of the words are their first letters, taken from each of the next five words

explanation.surface: A policeman of old begins timing his rounds on patrol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat' looks like the bobby's patrol route; it is a pulse. A bobby is a British police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong regular pulse, the same as a beat of the heart.

clue.text: Commonplace, a penny-farthing years ago

definitions.meaning: the Victorian high-wheeled bicycle was called by this name in its day

explanation.surface: An old high-wheeled bicycle was once an everyday sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal and unexceptional; and the period name for the big-wheeled bicycle, from the standard model.

clue.text: Extra purchase? Sounds like it

indicators.note: 'Sounds like it' says the word for purchase is heard spoken, giving a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: to buy is to purchase

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether an add-on is a further purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball is one of the extras.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched counts among the extras.

clue.text: Blush over a Conservative being intentionally offensive

indicators.note: in a down clue over means turned upside down, so the phrase for blush is read backwards

parts.note: to blush is to go red
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician reddens after making deliberately insulting remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks that belittle or disparage someone on purpose are derogatory.

clue.text: Ideal head of popular Spanish region

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so the opening letter of popular is taken

parts.note: Aragon is an autonomous region in north-east Spain

explanation.surface: The ideal leader of a well-liked region of Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a model of excellence, the perfect example of something.

clue.text: Ruminant studied, highly valued reportedly

indicators.note: 'reportedly' says the words studied and highly valued are to be taken as heard spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: to have read a subject is to have studied it, and dear means precious, highly valued, so the phrase spoken is read dear

explanation.surface: A cud-chewing animal that was researched and is prized, so people say.
explanation.definitionFit: This large deer chews the cud, and every cud-chewing mammal is a ruminant.

clue.text: In Wellington, buy exotic bird

indicators.note: something exotic is strange and foreign, so the letters are turned into an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: A shopper in New Zealand's capital purchases a rare foreign bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' looks like it describes the bird but it signals the anagram of WELLINGTON BUY.
explanation.definitionFit: This songbird, also called the yellowhammer, is a finch-like member of the bunting family.

clue.text: Having a cheerful outlook, popular goatherd worried about nothing

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the zero
worried means disturbed, so the letters of goatherd are jumbled

parts.note: the letter O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A well-liked shepherd frets over nothing yet stays upbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges GOATHERD and 'about' puts it round O, giving GOOD HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in good spirits, optimistic and cheerful.

clue.text: Jasper, perhaps a jester

definitions.meaning: black jasper is a kind of stone once rubbed with gold to test its purity
the clown in Shakespeare's As You Like It bears this name

explanation.surface: A man named Jasper might be a court jester.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jasper' looks like a man's name but is the stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A test stone for gold was often black jasper; Shakespeare named his fool in As You Like It after it.

clue.text: Gem in ring set by friend

parts.note: the letter O is round like a ring
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A jewel in a ring, mounted by a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: This iridescent mineral is a precious stone used in jewellery.

clue.text: Utterly depressed? True

parts.note: feeling down is feeling depressed
right means true or correct

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is completely depressed, and gets a yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb, the word means thoroughly or completely, as in plain rude.

clue.text: Staff employed by church

parts.note: to work for someone is to be employed by them
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Employees hired by the parish church.
explanation.definitionFit: The workforce is the body of employees, the staff of an organisation.

clue.text: To make light of note is easy at first

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter, taken from easy

explanation.surface: Downplaying a musical note is simple to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: To minimise a problem is to play it down, to treat it as unimportant.

clue.text: Singer's hit — score rearranged by producer, ultimately

indicators.note: 'rearranged' says the letters of hit and score are put in a new order
ultimately means at the end, so the final letter of producer is taken

explanation.surface: A vocalist's hit song had its score reworked by the record producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rearranged' makes CHORISTE from HIT SCORE, then R ends it; the 's is 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chorister is a member of a choir, especially a church choir, so a singer.

clue.text: Fell in chamber after retiring

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word for chamber is read backwards

parts.note: a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: Someone collapsed in the bedroom after going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' reads as a verb, but it is a noun: a hill or stretch of upland in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A fell is northern English for open upland, the same kind of wild high country as heath.

clue.text: Copper with most unusual habit

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters of most take a different order

explanation.surface: A policeman with a very odd habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a habitual practice, a usual way of behaving.

clue.text: Having plenty of money on respectable poker hand

indicators.note: in a down-style reading the second piece is placed on the first, so respectable comes before the money word

parts.note: straight means honest and respectable
flush means well supplied with cash

explanation.surface: A wealthy, upright gambler holds a winning poker hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, five cards in sequence and of one suit form one of the strongest hands.

clue.text: Woman upset after husband suggests dye

indicators.note: after means the woman's name comes after the husband letter
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the woman's name is read backwards

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A distressed woman follows her husband's suggestion to colour her hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish-brown colouring made from a plant, used on hair and skin.

clue.text: Wife dropped from golf club side

indicators.note: dropped from means taken out of, so the wife letter is removed from the club

parts.note: a wedge is a lofted golf club

explanation.surface: A wife has been axed from the golf club's team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' looks like a team to go with the club, but it is a border.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is the outer border or side of something.

clue.text: Round, helping to produce speech

parts.note: the letter O is round
a helping is a portion, a ration

explanation.surface: A round of drinks and a portion of food help someone get a speech out.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal address delivered to an audience.

clue.text: Bother American before function

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: Is it worth troubling an American before the party?
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: County's routine win

parts.note: a rut is a dull, fixed routine
to land a prize is to win it

explanation.surface: A county side records its usual victory.
explanation.walkthrough: RUTLAND is England's smallest historic county, in the East Midlands; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutland is a small English shire, an example of a county.

clue.text: Absolve former partner facing single charge

parts.note: an ex is a former husband, wife or partner
one is a single
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A judge clears an ex-spouse who faces just one count.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to free someone from blame, the legal sense of absolve.

clue.text: One identifies bishop and rook pocketed by small child

indicators.note: pocketed by means held inside, so the rook letter goes into the word for small child

parts.note: a mite is a small child
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A child pockets a bishop and a rook from the chess set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bishop' looks like a chess piece beside the rook, but the definition is the churchman's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's tall pointed headdress marks out the wearer's rank in the church.
